title: Cold rebuild: Audit sshd_config
summary: Rebuild Audit sshd_config from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Audit sshd_config** in *Hardening SSH*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: After a server rebuild, `ssh admin@10.20.1.10` prints `WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!` What's correct?
options: Confirm the new fingerprint out of band (console/admin); only then remove the old line with `ssh-keygen -R 10.20.1.10`
Ignore it; rebuilds always do that
steps.explain: A rebuild explains it, but so would an attacker. Verify, then replace only that entry.

steps.title: Rebuild Audit sshd_config cold
prompt: Write `List<string> Audit(string config)` (lines separated by `\n`). Each line is `Keyword value`; skip blanks and `#` comments; keywords are case-insensitive;
**the first occurrence of a keyword wins**. Return findings in this order:
- `"password login enabled"` unless PasswordAuthentication is `no` (default is yes)
- `"no AllowUsers"` if there's no AllowUsers line
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
